overall_assessment: Anonymization works well for NLA. No personal data is left in the 28 courses (the truncated tails of 4 were read from plans recomputed with the current R/anonymize.R), and a scan of all 311 NLA plans finds no e-mails, phones, staff names, contact blocks or year-stamped semester labels. All 10 suspects are false alarms. The phone flags are digit runs in URLs and identifiers (the NOU PDF path '20012001', the ScienceDirect PII 'S0361476X99910202'). The name_like flags are historical persons (Hans Nielsen Hauge, Herodes Antipas), programme and concept names (Global Journalism, Practical Theology, Stromme Foundation) and reading-list editors. Nearly all removals are the facts-box values 'Undervisningssemester: Vår/Høst' or 'Oppstart høst,' and 'Studieår: 2019 — 2020'. The two minor issues below are low severity.

findings.evidence: Semester of education: Autumn. Exception for academic year: Spring. … gjennomført [−studieåret 2019-2020.−] studieåret.
findings.description: Some sentences use an academic-year range as a condition. When the range is removed, the sentence says something different. 'Exception for academic year 2020-2021: Spring.' becomes 'Exception for academic year: Spring.', which reads as a permanent exception. The overlap rule '… IKF132 …, gjennomført studieåret 2019-2020.' becomes 'gjennomført studieåret.', and its condition is gone. Outside the packet, P320 has the same problem: 'når eksamen i P301 er avlagt studieåret 2013-2014 eller senere' becomes 'avlagt studieåret eller senere'. The rubric calls dangling text that now reads wrongly corruption. These are not harmless dangling labels, because the years scope a course rule. This affects 2 of 28 courses in the packet and 3 of 311 NLA plans.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R, .anon_generic(): the academic-year rules (str_replace_all with .not_gov_rule(...) and .drop_academic_year, for '/' and '-–—' ranges) remove every consecutive-year range from 1990 onwards wherever it occurs. The only exception is a government document named before it. A range that qualifies a past course or exam ('avlagt/gjennomført … studieåret YYYY-YYYY', '… eller senere') or an offering-specific exception sentence is not treated differently.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_generic(), add a guard like .not_gov: keep an academic-year range when 'gjennomført|avlagt|bestått|tatt' plus up to 20 characters plus 'studieåret' precedes it on the line, or when 'eller senere|eller tidligere|or later|or earlier' follows it. These years identify the course version a credit-reduction rule covers. Remove a whole sentence 'Exception for academic year YYYY-YYYY: <season>.' (an offering-specific notice) instead of only its year. Add tests in tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R for these three strings. If kept years count as content, record the change in methods.qmd.

findings.evidence: Start in the autumn, teaching over to semesters … Oppstart [−høst,−] undervisning over to semestere
findings.description: The two languages of the same facts-box field are handled differently. In the Norwegian value 'Oppstart høst, undervisning over to semestere', the season goes (38 removals across NLA). In the English value 'Start in the autumn, teaching over to semesters' (Teaching semester field, 3GJ322), it stays. The spec treats semester labels as administrative, and the pipeline strips this field's season everywhere else ('Teaching semester: Autumn' is removed in TAM321, TAM301 and 3GJ302). This is 1 of 311 NLA plans. The impact is negligible because the plan id ignores season words.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/anonymize.R, .anon_generic(): the season-after-label rule uses the lookbehind (?<=(?i:semester|undervisning|oppstart|startsemester|eksamen)[:\s]{0,3}). It matches 'Oppstart høst,' but not 'Start in the autumn,', where 'in the' separates the keyword from the season.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'start in the' to the lookbehind alternatives of the season-after-label rule (a fixed-length alternative, so it is valid in ICU). Add a test: anonymize_text('nla', 'Teaching semester:\nStart in the autumn, teaching over to semesters') should give 'Teaching semester:\nteaching over to semesters'.
